key_insight: AI models detected signals of vision-threatening diabetic retinopathy and advanced AMD in external eye photographs, while fairness training partially reduced demographic performance disparities.
clinical_relevance: External eye photography may offer a way to study posterior eye disease, but these proof-of-concept models are not yet suitable for clinical deployment.
method: Trained convolutional networks, a vision transformer, and a vision-language model to classify three eye diseases.
Evaluated discrimination using AUC and demographic fairness using equity-scaled AUC across sex, race, and ethnicity.
Applied five fairness-training strategies to the best-performing models.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used 40,687 photographs from 9,878 patients at Massachusetts Eye and Ear; baseline AUC reached 85.4% for vision-threatening diabetic retinopathy and 86.3% for advanced AMD, versus 67–74% for glaucoma.
watch_item: Single-center results and only partial disparity reduction leave generalizability and clinical readiness unresolved.
paper_title: Applications of Fairness Training in Artificial Intelligence to Ophthalmic Disease Diagnosis using External Eye Photographs
